books.section: Topic 4.4 America on the World Stage, A. Trade, Diplomacy, and the Expansion of American Influence

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the Oregon and Maine boundary settlements: Britain and the United States had shared the Oregon Country since 1818 under “joint occupation.” By the 1840s American settlers were pouring in along the Oregon Trail, and the cry “Fifty-four forty or fight” demanded the whole territory to the line of 54°40′ latitude. In 1846 President Polk, already at war with Mexico, compromised with Britain at the 49th parallel, the present border. Four years earlier, the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842 had settled a different border fight: it split the disputed land along the Maine–New Brunswick border after the bloodless “Aroostook War” of 1838–1839, and it closed the Caroline incident of 1837, in which British forces had burned an American ship, with both sides admitting wrongdoing.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Webster-Ashburton Treaty (1842) and the Oregon boundary settlement (1846). Paraphrased, not quoted; public domain sources.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note

rationales.A: The treaty split the disputed Maine land and closed the Caroline incident peacefully. Nothing in it prepares for war.
rationales.B: The treaty closed the incident with both sides admitting wrongdoing. That is a rebuke of the attack, not permission to repeat it.
rationales.C: A burned ship, a threatened execution, and a border standoff all ended in a treaty that split the land and shared the blame. Both governments chose a bargain over a war.
rationales.D: The Maine border was settled in 1842, but Oregon was still shared under joint occupation until the 1846 compromise.
rationales.general:
1. List what was at stake. A burned American ship, a Canadian sheriff threatened with execution, and disputed land in Maine.
2. Read the outcome. The treaty split the land and had both sides admit wrongdoing over the ship.
3. Put it together. Two governments with a war scare on their hands chose a negotiated settlement instead.
Background: The Aroostook War of 1838–1839 was bloodless brawling over the same disputed Maine land.
Remember: when both sides admit fault in a treaty, the treaty is the alternative to war.
